entry.title: What Is Serverless Architecture and When Does It Fail Enterprises?
entry.summary:
TL;DR
Serverless architecture shifts infrastructure responsibility to cloud providers, enabling event-driven, auto-scaling applications without direct server management.
It works best for bursty, unpredictable, or event-based workloads, where consumption pricing and rapid deployment create real efficiency gains.
It struggles under sustained, high-throughput systems, where per-invocation costs, latency variability, and performance unpredictability can outweigh benefits.
Operational complexity doesn’t disappear; it relocates, increasing the need for disciplined governance, observability, and architectural oversight.
Vendor lock-in risk rises with deep managed-service integration, limiting portability across cloud environments.
Hybrid cloud strategies often outperform pure serve…

entry.title: Social Media Feed at Scale A System Design Deep Dive — Question by Question
entry.summary:
Introduction
A social media feed seems simple on the surface — show the latest tweets from people you follow. But at 300 million users, it becomes one of the most challenging distributed systems problems in software engineering. This post walks through the real complexity challenge by challenge, including the wrong turns and how to navigate out of them. Interview Question: When millions of users open their feed simultaneously — how would you naively build it and where does that break down? Wrong Approach: For each user opening the app, fetch latest tweets from all 500 followed accounts iteratively using a for loop. Do this for all 300 million users opening the app. Why It Fails: Let us do the math. 300 million users multiplied by 500 followed accounts equals 150 billion database lookups …
